Ogulin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ogulin, Croatia

Not demolished. Ogulin's Jewish population, present from the 19th century and affiliated with the Jewish community of Karlovac, was always small, numbering 60 people in 1921 and just 24 by 1931; the community was deported to concentration camps during WWII and never recovered its former size, with only 25 Jews living in Ogulin by 1968. The town's most notable Jewish native was Vladimir Goldner (1933–2017), a physician and academic at the University of Zagreb's School of Medicine, who mentored ten master's and doctoral theses and was a member of the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts, the European Society of Cardiology, and the North American Society of Pacing and Electrophysiology. This private cemetery, established in 1880, still holds a few graves today, with tombstones ranging from 1889 to as recent as 2016.
